PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
  Process of Computation Problem Solving


•  This does not simply involve the act of computer programming.
•   It is a process, with programming being only one of the steps.
•  Before a program is written, a design for the program must be developed.
• And before a design can be developed, the problem to be solved must be well
  understood.
•  Once written, the program must be thoroughly tested.

  Process of Computation Problem Solving

Knowing what constitutes a solution.

  For some problems, there is only one solution. For others,
  there may be a number (or infinite number) of solutions.
  Thus, a problem may be stated as finding,

  • A solution

  • An approximate solution

  • A best solution

  •  All solutions

Describe Data and Algorithms



• For the MCGW problem, need to store the current state of the problem.


• When solving a computational problem, either suitable existing algorithms may be
 found, or new algorithms must be developed.

Source slide page 10 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 Process of Computation Problem Solving

Program Implementation

•  Design decisions provide general details of the data representation and the algorithmic
  approaches for solving a problem.
•  The details, however, do not specify which programming language to use, or how to
  implement the program.
•  Since we are programming in Python, the implementation needs to be expressed in a
   syntactically correct and appropriate way, using the instructions and features available in
   Python.

Source slide page 11 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 Process of Computation Problem Solving

Program Testing

Writing computer programs is difficult and challenging. As a result, programming errors are
pervasive, persistent and inevitable.

Given this fact, software testing is a crucial part of software development. Testing is done
incrementally as a program is being developed, when the program is complete, and when
the program needs to be updated.

NOTES.text:
Transcript block 1 (source interval 000000-000299 seconds):
[00:00:00.310] Hello everyone. Welcome back to the lecture series on Python for Computational Problem Solving.
[00:00:06.310] I am Neeta Anjieker from the Department of Computer Science and Engineering.
[00:00:11.600] In the previous video, we discussed what a computer hardware is and how information is stored internally or how it is represented in the computer hardware.
[00:00:23.540] In this lecture, we will look at what computer software is, what are the syntax and semantics and program translation that we would use to interact with the computer hardware.
[00:00:38.450] So what is a computer software? It is a set of program instructions and related data that can be executed by the computer. We need a computer software to tell the computer how exactly it should work.
[00:00:56.210] So it can be categorized into system software designed to provide a platform for your computer hardware and application software which performs a specific task like text editing or say playing games and so on.
[00:01:14.710] So let's look at this representation. You have the computer hardware on top of which you need an operating system to provide a platform on which the application software can reside.
[00:01:27.710] And as users, we would interact with the computer through various applications. So what exactly is an operating system?
[00:01:38.390] It is a software that manages and interacts with the hardware components of the computer.
[00:01:44.720] So, the operating system determines how to handle the memory, the main memory, the secondary memory, and how the CPU should function, or which application gets access to the CPU.
[00:01:58.220] An operating system is intrinsic to the operation of a computer, and that is why it is called the system software.
[00:02:07.320] It acts like a middleman by telling the application software whether it can run and how much of the storage it's available for use and what it does is it provides a user interface and a look and feel.
[00:02:24.020] So, when you use computers based on a Windows operating system, Mac operating system or Ubuntu, you will see that each of them have a different interface. They look and feel different. The way we access the files or the way we access the applications are different because of the operating system and the interface it provides to that particular computer hardware.
[00:02:51.990] So it determines how we interact with the computer.
[00:02:56.560] So let's look at this diagram here where I have the computer hardware and the system software houses the application software.
[00:03:05.660] Now you know that when you're using your Android phone even, you can...
[00:03:10.550] Install applications that work only on Android. If you are using an Apple phone, you can install applications that only work on iOS. So similarly, we have application softwares that are specific to certain applications.
[00:03:25.880] operating systems. So you can see here operating system takes care of file management, assembly, debugging, utilities and compilers and the application software are those which perform a specific task. So when I want to write a word document, I will use a specific application software like a word processing software.
[00:03:48.760] If I want to play games, I have to install that game on my operating system in order to play the desired game.
[00:03:56.760] So this is how we have application software through which I communicate with the system software and in turn access the resources of the computer hardware.
[00:04:10.870] Now that we know how it works, how exactly are we communicating with the hardware through the application and system software?
[00:04:19.860] So, when I am communicating with you, I have chosen English as a means of communication.
[00:04:26.360] Now, you are able to understand what I am saying because I am following the rules of the English language and that is why you understand it.
[00:04:36.530] So, you have syntax, semantics and a translation that takes place even when we are communicating with each other.
[00:04:45.530] So, let me explain that in detail.
[00:04:49.200] Now, programming languages are also called languages, right? But they are artificial languages because we are using that to communicate with a computer. And natural languages are what we use to communicate with each other, such as English. So, syntax and semantics are concepts that apply to all languages, whether they are natural or artificial.

Transcript block 2 (source interval 000300-000599 seconds):
[00:05:17.140] So, what exactly is syntax? Syntax is basically a set of rules that define the placement of the characters to form a valid sequence of those characters. So, in English, syntax would be the spellings of certain words that we use. So, syntax, English,
[00:05:39.860] For English include the letters of the alphabet, punctuation, and properly spelt words.
[00:05:46.360] You would notice that I just made an error when I was talking.
[00:05:50.780] So, when I say, hello there, how are you?
[00:05:54.680] You understand that sentence because it is a set of properly spelled words with properly used punctuations.
[00:06:04.680] You know that this is a question because I have used the question mark as a punctuation. Whereas, if I would write the same thing, hello there, how are you?
[00:06:23.970] is not how we pronounce the word how according to English language. So although it sounds right, it is not syntactically correct. So syntax tells you the rules of how to create these words and sentences. So what exactly is semantics? Semantics will tell you what these collection of words mean.
[00:06:49.810] So it's the meaning associated with the collection of syntactically correct sequence of characters.
[00:06:57.950] So look at the following sentence.
[00:07:00.340] Hello, are you how?
[00:07:02.340] That is syntactically correct because if you look at it, I have used the question mark at the end of the sentence and each of these words are spelled correctly.
[00:07:13.300] But does it make any sense? Is there meaning associated with it? No. Because this is now a syntactically correct sentence but semantically incorrect. Because I can't make out what it is. Right? So, every language has its own syntax and semantics. So, similarly, in programming also, when we're using or learning the Python programming language,
[00:07:38.430] We will see what are the syntax and semantics we have to use when we write programs.
[00:07:44.510] So, let's look at an example.
[00:07:49.750] In English, how is syntactically incorrect, but in Chinese, however, how is a valid word which means good.
[00:07:58.750] So you can see here, the syntax for English is how and has no meaning, but in Mandarin, how means good.
[00:08:06.750] And you can also see the syntax here, although the language is different, what I am trying to tell you is the pronunciation of the word has different semantics.
[00:08:18.350] for different languages. And that is what we would have to keep in mind when we write programs as well.
[00:08:25.980] So, when we communicate with the computer through a programming language, we know the CPU can only interpret machine code, which is your zeros and ones.
[00:08:39.630] So you can see here, all these zeros and ones is what the CPU understands. But can I write?
[00:08:46.900] Instructions as a collection of 0 and 1.
[00:08:50.030] It's going to be extremely difficult and I can make errors. Right? So writing programs in low level is very tedious and error prone because I may not understand what I've written at the end of it and it's so difficult to keep a track of each bit and bytes that I have used. And that is why we would use high level languages like Python, which is closer to our understanding.
[00:09:19.030] So since instructions are not in machine code we need a translator program. So for example if I start talking in a different language that you do not understand you would need a translator to tell you what I am trying to communicate. So similarly when I am writing a program in a high level language that the CPU does not understand I need a translator program.
[00:09:46.740] There are two types of translators. One is the compiler, which translates the entire code into machine code to be executed by the CPU, and the interpreter, which executes or interprets instructions one at a time.

Transcript block 3 (source interval 000600-000899 seconds):
[00:10:04.470] So how does it work? When I use a compiler as a translator, you can see here I have written a small program. Don't worry about the syntax or what exactly these mean.
[00:10:15.730] We will explore that when we write programs later on.
[00:10:19.230] So I've tried to add two numbers and find the sum.
[00:10:22.930] So the compiler would take this entire program, translate it, check the syntax semantics, convert it to machine code.
[00:10:31.950] And then it will give you the result. And this is how the compiler would work. Whereas an interpreter immediately execute instructions as they are entered. And this is referred to as an interactive mode. So when you give the program, the interpreter runs on top of the CPU where each and every line of code is interpreted, translated and executed immediately. And you see the results.
[00:11:00.670] one line at a time. So this is how your computer software works and how we can interact with the computer hardware. I hope you have understood all of this and we will meet in the next video to understand what programming language we are going to use and how exactly we would start writing your first computer program. Thank you.
